intro: Suriname is South America's smallest country and the only one where Dutch is the official language.

chapters.title: Dutch colony
text: Britain founded a colony, but in 1667 the Dutch took it in exchange for New Amsterdam, now New York. Plantations used enslaved Africans; many escaped into the forest and formed free Maroon communities that still exist.

highlight.title: New York swap
highlight.text: The Dutch gave up New Amsterdam, now New York, in exchange for Suriname.

chapters.title: Indenture
text: After slavery ended in 1863, workers came from India, Java (Indonesia) and China, creating one of the most diverse populations in the world.

chapters.title: Independence
text: Suriname became independent in 1975. Dési Bouterse led a military regime from 1980. In 2025 Jennifer Geerlings-Simons became the first woman president.

keyTerms.meaning: Descendants of people who escaped slavery.
